issue: CHANGELOG.md:43 says the change will "avoid quadratic backtracking when Codex failure diagnostics contain long whitespace runs after a status prefix". That status prefix was added earlier in this same unreleased PRD (codex_events.py:300), and the pre-PRD base had no such regex. Compared with the base, users see no change. Task 16 deleted an earlier entry of the same kind ("describes no change from the pre-PRD base"). Delete this entry too. The `fix` commit type seems to have forced the entry, so a follow-up `docs` commit can remove it

Some explicit status-code messages now classify as `unknown`. Before this change they classified correctly. Probed: `status=429`, `Error 429: Too Many Requests`, `HTTP error 503`, and bare reason-phrase forms like `429 Too Many Requests` and `503 Service Unavailable`. The spec allows numbers only in explicit HTTP/status/error-code context, and `status=429` and `Error 429:` are exactly that. Worse, tests/drivers/test_adapter_failure_classes.py:115 locks `status=429` and `Error 429:` in as `unknown`, so the wrong answer is now enforced as the expected class. Impact: a real 429 or 503 in these forms goes to the generic retry-then-PARK path instead of the bounded WAIT or rate-limit path. The native Codex forms ("unexpected status N", reqwest, HTTP/x) are covered.
